https://blog-assets.cloud.pennylane.ai/demos/tutorial_shors_algorithm_catalyst/main/_assets/images/qpe_full_combined_multi_est_wires.svg?w=1920 Demonstrating Pennylane-s circuit optimization technique called Catalyst. That is why the circuit does not look like usual Shors algorithm.

Introductory algorithm. Cirq represents qubits on their grid-based circuit. Users cand define the grid as they want. So the existence of grid does not necessarily indicate that it is a physical circuit. For example, here, X^0.5 is a logical gate that needs further decomposition and optimization. It is not yet fully decomposed. Thus, it is physical circuit only on the qubit side.
The shade is due to the selection (not the part of the circuit). https://quantumai.google/cirq/start/basics#unitary_matrices_and_decompositions (bottom snippet of this section).

The last circuit in the document. The #2-and internal circuit is just a grouped operation and its inside. The circuit inside, suppose as if there is another circuit that is being implanted into a larger circuit.
Figure 2.a. The heatmap at the bottom is not about a circuit, but the fidelity information of each gate with different parameter combinations.

The second snippet from: https://quantumai.google/cirq/experiments/fermi_hubbard/experiment_example#qubit_layout ; This is for some kind of physical simulation (Fermi-Hubbard). The arrows are for up-/down-spins, and numbers are for spin counts. This is actually one of the possible circuit layouts, so maybe this indicates a need for an ability to explore potentials.
